page.text:
The operations of pairing and union allow us to assemble finite
collections from existing elements, but they cannot escape the finite
realm if all starting sets are finite. The Axiom of the Power Set
provides an explosive leap in set-theoretic size: it asserts that all
possible subcollections of a set $A$ can be gathered into a new set
$\mathcal{P}(A)$. As Cantor's theorem will demonstrate, the power set of
any set is strictly greater in cardinality than the set itself.
